findings.reason: the section states a single capability that would ship twice with divergent behaviour; folding the command construction into one shared helper is a different deliverable and a different test than "add setup to the local branch".
findings.text: §2 makes project code able to run a script under a data system's setup commands and interpreter, but the local-vs-remote command construction is duplicated verbatim in `imas_codex/remote/executor.py:1171` (`executor.py:1234` local branch, `:1276` remote branch) and again in `executor.py:1321` (`:1396` local branch, `:1412` remote branch); adding a local setup path to one function leaves the other's local branch without it, so the new capability would hold only on whichever call path a caller happens to use. The design the brief should hand a node is one command-construction function both entry points call — and §2's own "Done when" would pass while the async path stayed broken.

findings.reason: two read paths over one archive will disagree about error classification, limits and caching, which is exactly the class of defect §5's own "decimated … never taken from the client's own flag" clause exists to prevent.
findings.text: §5 delivers a loader that reads a signal over a bounded window, while the repository already has one bounded signal read per data source: `imas_codex/discovery/signals/scanners/edas.py:598`, `mdsplus.py:334`, `ppf.py:206`, `jpf.py:204`, `tdi.py:109`, `imas.py:86` all implement `check()` returning samples for a reference window, and `imas_codex/remote/scripts/check_signals_batch.py` batches those reads with per-shot retry and error classification. The section adds a second read path with its own cache, limits and sampling semantics, and states no reason the connector's read cannot be the one `check()` and the loader both call.

findings.reason: the section can deliver the reduction (one saver, four call sites migrated) or add a fifth saver; the plan should state which, because "the save function these figures go through" is the difference between an owner and a parallel copy.
findings.text: §7 delivers "one function that draws the figure and refuses to write it", a fifth saver beside `scripts/codac_uda_prototype/loader.py:103` `_save_figure`, `scripts/figures_discovery_to_mapping.py:308` `save`, `scripts/figures_knowledge_graph_scale.py:697` `save` and `scripts/figures_icp_knowledge_map.py:1032` `save_gif`, with `plt.style.use("data-ink")` applied ad hoc in five scripts and no shared style module anywhere in the package. The owning mechanism to extend and make the single entry point is that shared save/style module — §7 creates the one that should replace the four, not one that joins them.

findings.reason: this is the one boundary that keeps facility lookup in one layer; a section that leaves it implicit is how the executor acquires a config lookup it is documented not to have.
findings.text: §2 resolves a data system's declared setup and interpreter, a resolution `imas_codex/remote/tools.py:165` `run_python_script` already performs through `resolve_remote_environment(_facility_config(facility), data_system)` and hands to the executor; the executor's own docstring says it "performs no facility lookup". A §2 that has the executor read facility config, or that adds a second facility-aware wrapper, forks the owner.

findings.reason: the plan must account for the surface it adds in its own text, either by naming a merged/retired tool or by stating why the read tool cannot fold into `search_signals` or `signal_analytics`.
findings.text: the supplied counts are public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0 (read 2026-11-15T00:46:10Z), yet §6 adds a new MCP tool (a facility read tool, absent in data-dictionary-only mode) and a corresponding refusal family (an endpoint or unbounded window is refused), and §2 adds a parameter to a public executor function; neither section names what it retires, merges, or why nothing can be. Today the server presents 30 tools (`imas_codex/llm/server.py`), each of which costs the client's context and the maintainer's surface.

findings.reason: §11 does name the alias's removal and its zero-consumer check, so the retirement is accounted for; the finding is recorded for the sequence, not as a design change.
findings.text: §10 keeps the old command as a transition alias "that resolves to the same code and the same single state root" and leaves its removal to §11; §10 therefore adds a CLI option (all three of distribution, branded command and MCP key) without naming what it retires, and the retirement of the alias is a second, later section's work, so the surface exists for the whole intervening period with no stated bound.

response_events.note: Section 2's done-when now requires the setup behaviour and the unchanged no-setup behaviour to hold on both the synchronous and the asynchronous entry point, with the negative control run on both.

Section 2 now states that facility and data-system resolution stays in the one facility-aware layer that already performs it, and the done-when requires that the executor still performs no facility lookup.

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — the design puts one archive client's behaviour behind four separate section-level surfaces (scanner, loader, MCP tool, name parser), each a shallow forwarder, where a single archive-client module taking an operation and returning a structured result is what all four need.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §7 delivers a fifth figure save function beside four existing ones, and §2's local-setup branch must not re-resolve facility environment that `remote/tools.py:165` already resolves.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0 (read 2026-11-15T00:46:10Z); §6 adds an MCP view and §2 adds an executor parameter, and neither section names anything it retires, merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the scanner registry (`discovery/signals/scanners/base.py`), the facility-aware script executor (`remote/tools.py:165` over `remote/executor.py:1171`) and `search_signals` (`llm/server.py:2413`) are the mechanisms §2/§4/§6 rightly extend, and the plan's §1 already names them; the two misses are recorded as findings below.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §5's loader re-implements a bounded signal read that the scanners' `check()` and `check_signals_batch.py` already perform, without saying why those cannot be extended.
